subject: Azure Partner Center referral signal canonicalization and field-seller mapping
body:
From: Gareth Lim <gareth.lim@microsoft.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: PartnerCenterOps <partnercenter-ops@microsoft.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: New referral export (Contoso) + canonical id proposal

Hi Ben / Vanessa,

Attached is the Partner Center export for Contoso inbound referrals for the last 90 days (pc_referrals_export_20261207.csv). We saw multiple referral signals for what looks like the same account: variations in company name and mismatched SellerContact emails. To speed up handoff to your field sellers we propose adding a canonical referral_id field (msft_pc_canonical_id) that maps to either a Salesforce account id or a persistent Contoso tenant id.

Can Redwood ingest that canonical id on intake and use it to: 1) dedupe referrals, 2) attach pending referrals to a single Owner candidate, and 3) surface a preferred seller contact in your Console?

Happy to run through the CSV this afternoon if useful.

Thanks,
Gareth
Partner Center - Referral Integrations
Microsoft

----
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Gareth Lim <gareth.lim@microsoft.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: New referral export (Contoso) + canonical id proposal

Gareth — thanks for the export. Quick notes after a skim:

- We can ingest msft_pc_canonical_id, but we need a deterministic matching rule to tie it to our SFDC AccountId or our internal account_fingerprint.
- Two practical questions: will Partner Center populate canonical_id for historical referrals (backfill), and will the canonical_id be stable across duplicate referrals from different MSFT sellers?
- The bigger operational ask: when canonical_id maps to multiple in-field seller owners in SFDC, what routing rule should win? We need a primary consent flag or a last-touch timestamp.

I'm proposing a short mapping template (attached: proposed-mapping-v1.xlsx) that includes: canonical_id, partnercenter_referral_id, sfdc_account_id, msft_seller_email, redwood_owner_candidate, seller_consent_status. If we agree on fields I can drop a one-click ingestion job into our intake pipeline.

I'll schedule a 30-min sync for 3pm PT — Vanessa, Karthik, Jordan, please confirm availability.

— Ben
Account Executive, GTM Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs:
- proposed-mapping-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 72KB)

----
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: New referral export (Contoso) + canonical id proposal

Thanks Ben & Gareth. Quick constraints from field ops:

- Field sellers will only accept handoffs with a single, verifiable contact (email + phone). If canonical_id points to multiple contacts we need a highlighted primary contact.
- Consent: MSFT seller consent must surface as a boolean and a timestamp. If consent is older than 90 days, we require re-consent before handoff.
- SLA: prefer that Redwood route to the 'preferred owner' but also maintain a fallback list of at most two alternate owners. The fallback order should be: (1) SP leader assigned in SFDC, (2) most recent MSFT last-touch.

I approve the proposed-mapping-v1 fields with the addition of seller_consent_timestamp and contact_phone. I'll be on the 3pm sync.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partner GTM
Redwood Inference
